name: Nebraska Eats: Restaurants
subtitle: Steaks, Reubens & Taquerías
description:
Nebraska's restaurants, from the Stockyards steakhouse that has served Omaha since 1922 to tacos on South 24th Street.

Nebraska Eats is a free guide to eating in Nebraska: 12 steakhouses, 7 places for a Reuben or a cheese frenchee and 4 South Omaha taquerías we checked by hand, plus 4,809 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 398 towns, from Omaha and Lincoln to Grand Island, Kearney, North Platte and Scottsbluff. No account, no ads.

NEBRASKA GUIDES
• Steakhouses: every one the Flatwater Free Press reviewed or ranked in its 2025 steakhouse series, from Johnny's Cafe and Gorat's to Chances R in York.
• Reubens & Frenchees: Omaha's Reubens (the city claims the sandwich; New York does too) and Lincoln's cheese frenchee.
• South Omaha Taquerías: tacos on and around South 24th Street.
• Oldest Places: 5 places open at their address since 1960 or earlier, back to Glur's Tavern in 1876.
• James Beard Honors: 6 honored Nebraska restaurants.

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "prime rib", "reuben", "frenchee".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in fall 2026 against a dated 2025 or 2026 story or a visitor bureau's own page or listing. The rest come from Overture Maps open data and the Nebraska Liquor Control Commission's Active License Roster: a place matched to an on-sale license says it serves alcohol, and anywhere else that's unknown, never no. The app shows no inspection results and computes no grades; each place links to the state's page on who inspects where. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings. Newer restaurant data downloads from the Nebraska Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the State of Nebraska, the Nebraska Liquor Control Commission or the Nebraska Department of Agriculture), Visit Omaha or any visitor bureau, the University of Nebraska or any team, or the James Beard Foundation. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: Nebraska Eats is a free guide to restaurants in Nebraska (the U.S. state). Its focus is the state's own food: steakhouses, Omaha's Reubens and Lincoln's cheese frenchees, and South Omaha's taquerías, 24 places checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source, plus the James Beard honorees and the oldest places. It also lists 4,809 restaurants, cafés and bars in 398 towns from open map data and the state's liquor-license roster. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Steakhouses (or Reubens & Frenchees, South Omaha Taquerías, James Beard Honors, Oldest Places, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it. A place matched to the Nebraska Liquor Control Commission's roster shows its license as published; the app shows no inspection results or grades and links to the Nebraska Department of Agriculture's page on who inspects where.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("prime rib", "reuben", "frenchee").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside Nebraska (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on Nebraska, and distance sorting still works from where you are.

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the Nebraska Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); the Nebraska Liquor Control Commission's Active License Roster (public record; license numbers and types only, never licensee or manager names); James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites, local news and visitor-bureau pages.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/nebraska-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers Nebraska; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution in the app.
